definition: Additional computation applied at inference time (rather than during training) to improve a model's output quality, such as generating and evaluating multiple reasoning paths.
details: Increasing test-time compute — for example, through extended chain-of-thought reasoning or self-verification — has emerged as an important lever for improving model performance on hard problems, complementing gains from scaling training compute.
story: Imagine a sketch artist who starts with static and, stroke by stroke, sharpens it into a face. Think of it this way: Additional computation applied at inference time (rather than during training) to improve a model's output quality, such as generating and evaluating multiple reasoning paths. And here is the clever part: Increasing test-time compute — for example, through extended chain-of-thought reasoning or self-verification — has emerged as an important lever for improving model performance on hard problems, complementing gains from scaling training compute. The model dreams a little, then cleans up the dream. And that is Test-Time Compute — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.
